jobs.title: Executive Director, Institutional Sales - West Coast
jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley Investment Management (MSIM) is one of the largest global asset management organizations of any full-service securities firm, with more than 50 years of history, a presence in 26 countries, and a total of $1.9 trillion in assets under management as of March 31, 2026.

MSIM provides broad-based specialization across a range of asset classes in public and private markets. Our independent investment teams leverage Morgan Stanley’s global resources to serve a diverse client base of governments, institutions, corporations, advisors and individuals worldwide. Our investment solutions include a broad range of alternatives, high-conviction active strategies, customization strategies, ESG expertise and tax management solutions. For further information about Morgan Stanley Investment Management, please visit www.morganstanley.com/im

The North American Institutional Sales Team
is responsible for driving growth across the MSIM suite of investment capabilities through the development of new relationships, the enhancement of existing relationships, and the application of a holistic and partnership-oriented approach to provide a best-in- client experience.

Expanding our institutional client coverage on the West Coast, the Executive Director will focus on driving fundraising results across the MSIM’s platform - equities, fixed income, private credit, private equity, private real assets, and hedge funds. Joining a collaborative team, this individual will be responsible for cultivating and managing relationships with institutional clients. The team works in close partnership with consultant relations and investment teams to deliver the full breadth of MSIM’s investment ideas and solutions to clients.

Responsibilities

Develop and maintain relationships with institutional asset owners across the West Coast region of the United States, across all client segmentations – public pensions, corporate pensions, insurance, endowments, foundations, and healthcare systems.
Cultivate strong partnerships across key internal stakeholder groups, including Consultant Relations, Product Specialists, Marketing and Portfolio Management, to support strategy execution and fund marketing initiatives.
Maintain detailed knowledge of investment strategies across public and private markets to effectively position solutions to clients.
Understand clients' investment objectives and provide tailored solutions to meet their needs.
Provide mentorship and guidance to junior professionals and support the continued development of the organization’s talent base.

Requirements

Minimum of 8 years of experience developing new client relationships at an asset management platform, with exposure to both public and private markets asset classes.
History of helping successfully build and maintain client relationships with sophisticated asset owners.
Strong understanding of institutional sales processes, including best practices working with consultant coverage and investment teams.
Understanding of institutional segments such as corporate defined benefit, public pension systems, insurance, endowments, foundations, and healthcare systems.
Investment and markets acumen with the ability to synthesize, distill, and articulate investment strategies in a straightforward manner.
Excellent communication skills, both written and presentation skills.
Strong organizational skills.
Results-oriented thinker who embraces accountability.
Success working in a highly collaborative environment.
Enthusiasm to travel as needed.
FINRA Series 7 and 63 required.

Who You Are

Operates with a strong sense of ethics and integrity in your interactions with others and decision making.
Takes accountability and ownership in your work with a focus on long-term value creation.
Track record of fostering a culture of honesty, transparency and accountability within teams.
Proven ability to collaborate across teams to deliver optimal solutions for clients.
A passion for innovation, with a continuous improvement mindset to drive excellence.
Respect for individual differences, with an openness to diverse perspectives.
Engagement in community service, volunteering or corporate citizenship initiatives.
Commitment to mentoring and supporting professional growth of others.

What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser.

Expected base pay rates for the role will be between $200,000 and $300,000 per year at the commencement of employment. However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs.

Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents.

Our workforce reflects a broad cross-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Scion Executive Search
has been engaged to conduct the search for a Chief Operating Officer for Spectrum360, a leading Northern New Jersey nonprofit providing special education, adult services, and enrichment programs for people with autism and related disabilities. This is a pivotal opportunity for an experienced enterprise operator and people leader to strengthen a complex, mission-driven organization and help expand its capacity for long-term impact.

ABOUT SPECTRUM360:

Established in 1961, Spectrum360 provides education, socialization, therapeutic support, and pathways to greater independence for children, young adults, and adults with autism and related disabilities. Across multiple Northern New Jersey campuses,
Spectrum360’s programs create a continuum of support that evolves alongside the approximately 500 individuals it serves.

Through Academy360 and Path360, students ages 3 through 21 receive individualized education while building the skills and confidence needed for adulthood. Independence360 carries that commitment forward through day habilitation, vocational development, and opportunities for greater independence, while FilmAcademy360 and CulinaryAcademy360 provide creative, hands-on pathways for individuals to discover their strengths, develop new capabilities, and connect with their communities.

Spectrum360 is entering an important phase of organizational development. Its programs are strong and demand remains significant. The next Chief Operating Officer will help the organization build the leadership capacity, operational discipline, and cross-functional alignment needed to sustain quality, navigate complexity, and create room for thoughtful growth.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officer will serve as a senior enterprise leader with responsibility for the integration, effectiveness, and continuous improvement of Spectrum360's school and adult-service operations. The COO will connect program realities with organizational strategy, ensuring that decisions are grounded in service quality, regulatory requirements, workforce needs, financial sustainability, and the practical realities of a complex, multi-site organization.

This is not a conventional desk-based operations role. The COO must move fluently between enterprise priorities and immediate operational decisions, handling complex exceptions while strengthening the systems, leaders, and decision-making structures that allow routine work to occur closer to the point of service. The role requires a leader who can see patterns, surface blind spots, and bring clarity to situations where competing needs do not produce an obvious answer.

The successful candidate will pair rigor with humanity. They will establish accountability, develop leaders, and advance cultural change without losing the trust of a long-tenured and deeply mission-committed workforce. They will be a candid, solutions-oriented partner to the CEO and a credible leader across clinical, educational, administrative, and operational teams.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Enterprise Operations and Organizational Integration

Lead the effective integration of school, adult-service, admissions, facilities, technology, and related operational functions across Spectrum360's campuses.
Translate organizational strategy into clear operating priorities, decision rights, accountability structures, and practical execution plans.
Strengthen communication and coordination across programs and shared services so that information reaches the right people and issues are resolved at the appropriate level.
Balance near-term operating demands with sustained attention to organizational development, service quality, and long-term readiness.
Build durable institutional knowledge, incident-response discipline, and continuity across critical operating processes without creating unnecessary complexity.

People Leadership and Culture

Lead, coach, and develop senior program and operational leaders, strengthening their ability to manage performance, exercise judgment, and lead through change.
Advance a culture of transparency, teamwork, accountability, and respectful communication across a workforce with varied professional backgrounds and levels of experience.
Address performance and organizational issues directly while using sound judgment, empathy, and an incremental approach that builds sustainable commitment.
Partner closely with Human Resources to strengthen management practices, succession depth, talent development, and employee engagement.
Clarify and reinforce reporting relationships and chain-of-command expectations while remaining accessible and responsive to staff.

Financial Stewardship and Strategic Growth

Bring an analytical, operational perspective to budgeting, forecasting, staffing models, enrollment planning, and resource allocation.
Test assumptions, identify financial and operational blind spots, and ensure that program plans are grounded in historical performance, demand, capacity, and cost realities.
Partner with the CEO, finance leadership, and program leaders to evaluate growth opportunities, new service models, and revenue diversification initiatives.
Help create the leadership and operating capacity required for Spectrum360 to serve more individuals and pursue mission-aligned expansion responsibly.

Quality, Risk and Regulatory Leadership

Maintain disciplined oversight of program quality, safety, security, compliance, and risk across education and adult-service environments.
Ensure policies and procedures are clear, usable, consistently applied, and proportionate to the risks they are intended to address.
Exercise sound judgment in complex personnel, regulatory, and operational situations where precedent and organization-wide implications must be considered.
Guide effective response to critical incidents and ensure that lessons learned translate into practical improvement.

Executive Partnership and Governance

Serve as a trusted operating partner to the CEO, bringing concise analysis, clear recommendations, and candid counsel.
Escalate the right issues at the right time, keeping the CEO informed without shifting routine operational decisions upward.
Help distinguish management decisions from matters requiring board visibility or action and represent operational priorities to the Board when requested.
Model integrity, discretion, shared accountability, and organizational loyalty across all leadership relationships.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Significant senior leadership experience in a complex, multi-site, regulated direct service organization. Relevant settings may include disability services, behavioral health, healthcare, human services, education, or adjacent mission-driven environments.
Demonstrated responsibility for substantial programs, operations, and workforces at a scale comparable to Spectrum360.
Evidence of strengthening an under-structured, rapidly growing, or operationally challenged organization while maintaining service continuity and trust.
Proven success developing leaders, elevating management performance, and creating a culture of accountability among both emerging and long-tenured staff.
Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to evaluate budgets, operating models, staffing assumptions, program economics, and growth opportunities.
Experience operating within meaningful regulatory, compliance, safety, and quality requirements. Familiarity with New Jersey special education or developmental disability systems is valued but not required.
Credibility leading clinical, educational, or other professional service teams is essential.
Exceptional judgment, communication, listening, conflict-management, and problem-solving skills.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or relevant professional credentials preferred.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Spectrum360 will offer a competitive executive compensation and benefits package. The anticipated salary for this role is $200,000 commensurate with experience and qualifications. Relocation support may be considered for the selected candidate.

Applications and Nominations:

Spectrum360 has retained Scion Executive Search, a national executive search firm specializing in nonprofit recruitment, to lead this search. Review of applications, nominations, and expressions of interest will begin immediately and continue on a confidential basis until an appointment is made. For immediate consideration, please apply with your resume and cover letter formatted in Microsoft Word, via: https://scionexecutivesearch.com/job/15355/

Please Address Applications to:

Sydney Burnham

Scion Executive Search

Scion Executive Search is an award-winning retained executive search firm. Our track record and recruitment process have made us one of the top recruitment firms in the United States. Through innovative team building and recruitment solutions, Scion Executive Search seamlessly bridges the gap in interim and executive searches. Our track record and recruitment process have made us one of the top recruitment firms in the nation.

jobs.description:
Company Description
Norwalk ACTS is a collective impact organization dedicated to transforming local systems so that every child and young person in Norwalk, CT can thrive. The organization focuses on aligning resources, policies, practices, and power structures to actively dismantle racism and drive equitable outcomes. Working across sectors, Norwalk ACTS brings together schools, community organizations, families, and civic leaders to advance educational and developmental equity. Team members contribute to an environment that values collaboration, data-informed decision making, and community voice. The organization is ideal for individuals committed to social justice, equity, and systemic change.
Role Description
The Director of Development is a full-time, hybrid role based in Norwalk, CT, with flexibility for some work from home. This role leads the creation and execution of a comprehensive fundraising strategy that supports Norwalk ACTS’ mission and long-term sustainability. Day-to-day responsibilities include cultivating and stewarding individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations; managing annual giving campaigns; and overseeing planned giving initiatives as appropriate. The Director of Development will prepare and monitor development budgets, coordinate fundraising events, and ensure accurate tracking of gifts and donor data. This position collaborates closely with the executive team and program staff to align fundraising priorities with organizational goals and to develop compelling cases for support. The role also includes preparing reports for leadership and the board, and communicating impact to stakeholders through proposals, presentations, and donor outreach.
Qualifications

Demonstrated experience in fundraising, philanthropy, and donor stewardship, with a track record of meeting or exceeding revenue goals.
Knowledge of annual giving and planned giving strategies, including donor segmentation, campaigns, and legacy giving approaches.
Strong budgeting and financial management skills, including the ability to develop, monitor, and report on development-related budgets.
Experience designing and implementing comprehensive development plans, including events, campaigns, and relationship-building activities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to craft compelling narratives that connect donors to mission and impact.
Ability to build and maintain inclusive, trust-based relationships with diverse stakeholders, including donors, board members, partners, and community members.
Strong organizational and project management skills, with attention to detail and ability to manage multiple deadlines.
Commitment to racial equity, social justice, and systemic change, and willingness to engage in ongoing learning and reflection.
Proficiency with donor management/CRM systems and standard office software; experience using data to inform fundraising strategy is preferred.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in nonprofit management, business, communications, or a related field; prior experience in a development leadership role is highly beneficial.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Facilities (SY26-27)
jobs.description:
Position Overview

Boston Public Schools (BPS) is the largest school district in Massachusetts, serving approximately 50,000 students with a $1.2 billion budget. The Office of Facilities Management (OFM) is one of the largest departments within the district, managing a $90 million annual budget (approximately 10% of total spending). The department is responsible for maintaining 125 school facilities across 11 million square feet, ensuring the safety and functionality of educational spaces. Additionally, OFM is involved in the district's Long-Term Facilities Plan, focusing on strategic capital upgrades and improvements across the district.

The Executive Director of Facilities Management will provide overall leadership for the planning, implementation, and management of facilities maintenance, operations, planning, engineering, minor and major projects. The Executive Director will report directly to the Chief of Operations and will play a critical role in ensuring the health, safety, and security of all school facilities, thereby fostering a positive learning environment. The successful candidate will excel in managing relationships, systems, and processes, setting priorities, and negotiating effectively.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Staff Management

Establish departmental goals and objectives aligned with district mission and strategic priorities.
Monitor and evaluate staff performance, providing feedback, support, and opportunities for professional development.
Hire, assign work, and establish clear performance expectations for staff. Take corrective action when necessary, including managing grievances and disciplinary processes.
Foster a positive, collaborative work environment and build a strong, effective team.

Operational & Budget Management

Develop and manage the departmental budget in collaboration with assigned budget analysts. Ensure adherence to fiscal controls, district policies, and regulatory requirements.
Oversee daily operations, including custodial and grounds administration, building systems maintenance, and projects team.
Ensure efficient allocation of resources and prioritize maintenance activities based on district needs and operational requirements.
Coordinate and manage work requests, estimates, and prioritization of repair and replacement needs for district facilities.

Facilities Planning & Maintenance

Provide oversight of maintenance and capital planning efforts, ensuring facilities are safe, clean, and conducive to learning.
Monitor ongoing maintenance projects and ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local building codes and safety regulations.
Conduct research into new maintenance techniques, trends, and technologies to improve efficiency and productivity.
Oversee the district's Long-Term Facilities Plan, focusing on capital improvements and major renovations to ensure the long-term sustainability of BPS facilities.

Compliance & Regulatory Oversight

Interpret and ensure compliance with all relevant laws, codes, and regulations, including those related to building codes, purchasing, prevailing wages, and safety standards.
Administer projects to ensure all work adheres to safety standards and regulatory codes.

Collaboration & Communication

Collaborate with district departments, city partners, external agencies, and contractors to coordinate facility-related activities.
Serve as a member of the district bargaining team for labor negotiations involving facility operations personnel.
Provide counsel and technical support to district staff regarding maintenance strategies, priorities, and best practices.
Communicate regularly with stakeholders to gather feedback on staff performance and overall customer satisfaction with facilities services.

Qualifications:

Required

Bachelor's degree in facilities management, engineering, or a related field.
At least ten years of increasingly responsible experience in facilities management, construction, or a related field, preferably in an educational or public service setting.

Preferred

Master’s degree in a related field.

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of custodial and grounds administration, facilities maintenance, building systems, and construction.
Expertise in facilities planning, design, construction, and capital improvement projects.
Familiarity with federal, state, and local building codes, safety standards, and regulations.
Strong proficiency with standard office software (e.g., spreadsheets, word processing) and facility management tools.
Proven ability to develop and manage departmental budgets, ensuring adherence to fiscal controls and policies.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to effectively manage relationships, collaborate across departments, and lead a diverse team.
Skilled in prioritizing tasks, setting goals, and managing multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Take individual initiative and accept responsibility and be held accountable.
Ability to adapt to change, innovate, and remain flexible in a dynamic environment.

Additional Qualities

Commitment to maintaining a positive learning environment through the proactive and efficient management of facilities.
Ability to negotiate and resolve conflicts effectively, ensuring that the needs of all stakeholders are met.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and build teams to achieve organizational goals.

The Executive Director of Facilities Management will play a pivotal role in ensuring that BPS facilities meet the highest standards of safety, cleanliness, and functionality, supporting the district’s commitment to providing a positive educational experience for all students.

Terms:

Managerial Tier: E81
Employment Type: Managerial
Work Schedule: 8am – 4pm with peak periods; evening and weekend availability as necessary.

new_jobs.description:
Scion Executive Search
has been engaged to conduct the search for a Chief Operating Officer for Spectrum360, a leading Northern New Jersey nonprofit providing special education, adult services, and enrichment programs for people with autism and related disabilities. This is a pivotal opportunity for an experienced enterprise operator and people leader to strengthen a complex, mission-driven organization and help expand its capacity for long-term impact.

ABOUT SPECTRUM360:

Established in 1961, Spectrum360 provides education, socialization, therapeutic support, and pathways to greater independence for children, young adults, and adults with autism and related disabilities. Across multiple Northern New Jersey campuses,
Spectrum360’s programs create a continuum of support that evolves alongside the approximately 500 individuals it serves.

Through Academy360 and Path360, students ages 3 through 21 receive individualized education while building the skills and confidence needed for adulthood. Independence360 carries that commitment forward through day habilitation, vocational development, and opportunities for greater independence, while FilmAcademy360 and CulinaryAcademy360 provide creative, hands-on pathways for individuals to discover their strengths, develop new capabilities, and connect with their communities.

Spectrum360 is entering an important phase of organizational development. Its programs are strong and demand remains significant. The next Chief Operating Officer will help the organization build the leadership capacity, operational discipline, and cross-functional alignment needed to sustain quality, navigate complexity, and create room for thoughtful growth.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officer will serve as a senior enterprise leader with responsibility for the integration, effectiveness, and continuous improvement of Spectrum360's school and adult-service operations. The COO will connect program realities with organizational strategy, ensuring that decisions are grounded in service quality, regulatory requirements, workforce needs, financial sustainability, and the practical realities of a complex, multi-site organization.

This is not a conventional desk-based operations role. The COO must move fluently between enterprise priorities and immediate operational decisions, handling complex exceptions while strengthening the systems, leaders, and decision-making structures that allow routine work to occur closer to the point of service. The role requires a leader who can see patterns, surface blind spots, and bring clarity to situations where competing needs do not produce an obvious answer.

The successful candidate will pair rigor with humanity. They will establish accountability, develop leaders, and advance cultural change without losing the trust of a long-tenured and deeply mission-committed workforce. They will be a candid, solutions-oriented partner to the CEO and a credible leader across clinical, educational, administrative, and operational teams.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Enterprise Operations and Organizational Integration

Lead the effective integration of school, adult-service, admissions, facilities, technology, and related operational functions across Spectrum360's campuses.
Translate organizational strategy into clear operating priorities, decision rights, accountability structures, and practical execution plans.
Strengthen communication and coordination across programs and shared services so that information reaches the right people and issues are resolved at the appropriate level.
Balance near-term operating demands with sustained attention to organizational development, service quality, and long-term readiness.
Build durable institutional knowledge, incident-response discipline, and continuity across critical operating processes without creating unnecessary complexity.

People Leadership and Culture

Lead, coach, and develop senior program and operational leaders, strengthening their ability to manage performance, exercise judgment, and lead through change.
Advance a culture of transparency, teamwork, accountability, and respectful communication across a workforce with varied professional backgrounds and levels of experience.
Address performance and organizational issues directly while using sound judgment, empathy, and an incremental approach that builds sustainable commitment.
Partner closely with Human Resources to strengthen management practices, succession depth, talent development, and employee engagement.
Clarify and reinforce reporting relationships and chain-of-command expectations while remaining accessible and responsive to staff.

Financial Stewardship and Strategic Growth

Bring an analytical, operational perspective to budgeting, forecasting, staffing models, enrollment planning, and resource allocation.
Test assumptions, identify financial and operational blind spots, and ensure that program plans are grounded in historical performance, demand, capacity, and cost realities.
Partner with the CEO, finance leadership, and program leaders to evaluate growth opportunities, new service models, and revenue diversification initiatives.
Help create the leadership and operating capacity required for Spectrum360 to serve more individuals and pursue mission-aligned expansion responsibly.

Quality, Risk and Regulatory Leadership

Maintain disciplined oversight of program quality, safety, security, compliance, and risk across education and adult-service environments.
Ensure policies and procedures are clear, usable, consistently applied, and proportionate to the risks they are intended to address.
Exercise sound judgment in complex personnel, regulatory, and operational situations where precedent and organization-wide implications must be considered.
Guide effective response to critical incidents and ensure that lessons learned translate into practical improvement.

Executive Partnership and Governance

Serve as a trusted operating partner to the CEO, bringing concise analysis, clear recommendations, and candid counsel.
Escalate the right issues at the right time, keeping the CEO informed without shifting routine operational decisions upward.
Help distinguish management decisions from matters requiring board visibility or action and represent operational priorities to the Board when requested.
Model integrity, discretion, shared accountability, and organizational loyalty across all leadership relationships.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Significant senior leadership experience in a complex, multi-site, regulated direct service organization. Relevant settings may include disability services, behavioral health, healthcare, human services, education, or adjacent mission-driven environments.
Demonstrated responsibility for substantial programs, operations, and workforces at a scale comparable to Spectrum360.
Evidence of strengthening an under-structured, rapidly growing, or operationally challenged organization while maintaining service continuity and trust.
Proven success developing leaders, elevating management performance, and creating a culture of accountability among both emerging and long-tenured staff.
Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to evaluate budgets, operating models, staffing assumptions, program economics, and growth opportunities.
Experience operating within meaningful regulatory, compliance, safety, and quality requirements. Familiarity with New Jersey special education or developmental disability systems is valued but not required.
Credibility leading clinical, educational, or other professional service teams is essential.
Exceptional judgment, communication, listening, conflict-management, and problem-solving skills.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or relevant professional credentials preferred.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Spectrum360 will offer a competitive executive compensation and benefits package. The anticipated salary for this role is $200,000 commensurate with experience and qualifications. Relocation support may be considered for the selected candidate.

Position Overview

Boston Public Schools (BPS) is the largest school district in Massachusetts, serving approximately 50,000 students with a $1.2 billion budget. The Office of Facilities Management (OFM) is one of the largest departments within the district, managing a $90 million annual budget (approximately 10% of total spending). The department is responsible for maintaining 125 school facilities across 11 million square feet, ensuring the safety and functionality of educational spaces. Additionally, OFM is involved in the district's Long-Term Facilities Plan, focusing on strategic capital upgrades and improvements across the district.

The Executive Director of Facilities Management will provide overall leadership for the planning, implementation, and management of facilities maintenance, operations, planning, engineering, minor and major projects. The Executive Director will report directly to the Chief of Operations and will play a critical role in ensuring the health, safety, and security of all school facilities, thereby fostering a positive learning environment. The successful candidate will excel in managing relationships, systems, and processes, setting priorities, and negotiating effectively.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Staff Management

Establish departmental goals and objectives aligned with district mission and strategic priorities.
Monitor and evaluate staff performance, providing feedback, support, and opportunities for professional development.
Hire, assign work, and establish clear performance expectations for staff. Take corrective action when necessary, including managing grievances and disciplinary processes.
Foster a positive, collaborative work environment and build a strong, effective team.

Operational & Budget Management

Develop and manage the departmental budget in collaboration with assigned budget analysts. Ensure adherence to fiscal controls, district policies, and regulatory requirements.
Oversee daily operations, including custodial and grounds administration, building systems maintenance, and projects team.
Ensure efficient allocation of resources and prioritize maintenance activities based on district needs and operational requirements.
Coordinate and manage work requests, estimates, and prioritization of repair and replacement needs for district facilities.

Facilities Planning & Maintenance

Provide oversight of maintenance and capital planning efforts, ensuring facilities are safe, clean, and conducive to learning.
Monitor ongoing maintenance projects and ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local building codes and safety regulations.
Conduct research into new maintenance techniques, trends, and technologies to improve efficiency and productivity.
Oversee the district's Long-Term Facilities Plan, focusing on capital improvements and major renovations to ensure the long-term sustainability of BPS facilities.

Compliance & Regulatory Oversight

Interpret and ensure compliance with all relevant laws, codes, and regulations, including those related to building codes, purchasing, prevailing wages, and safety standards.
Administer projects to ensure all work adheres to safety standards and regulatory codes.

Collaboration & Communication

Collaborate with district departments, city partners, external agencies, and contractors to coordinate facility-related activities.
Serve as a member of the district bargaining team for labor negotiations involving facility operations personnel.
Provide counsel and technical support to district staff regarding maintenance strategies, priorities, and best practices.
Communicate regularly with stakeholders to gather feedback on staff performance and overall customer satisfaction with facilities services.

Qualifications:

Required

Bachelor's degree in facilities management, engineering, or a related field.
At least ten years of increasingly responsible experience in facilities management, construction, or a related field, preferably in an educational or public service setting.

Preferred

Master’s degree in a related field.

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of custodial and grounds administration, facilities maintenance, building systems, and construction.
Expertise in facilities planning, design, construction, and capital improvement projects.
Familiarity with federal, state, and local building codes, safety standards, and regulations.
Strong proficiency with standard office software (e.g., spreadsheets, word processing) and facility management tools.
Proven ability to develop and manage departmental budgets, ensuring adherence to fiscal controls and policies.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to effectively manage relationships, collaborate across departments, and lead a diverse team.
Skilled in prioritizing tasks, setting goals, and managing multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Take individual initiative and accept responsibility and be held accountable.
Ability to adapt to change, innovate, and remain flexible in a dynamic environment.

Additional Qualities

Commitment to maintaining a positive learning environment through the proactive and efficient management of facilities.
Ability to negotiate and resolve conflicts effectively, ensuring that the needs of all stakeholders are met.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and build teams to achieve organizational goals.

new_jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by delivering solutions that improve communities and enhance quality of life. As the Program Manager, Deputy Director
for our client’s Residential Construction Department (RCD)
, you'll lead the planning and delivery of large-scale residential development and housing revitalization programs across Florida
, helping create safe, sustainable, and thriving communities.

In this role, you'll oversee complex residential initiatives that include the rehabilitation, reconstruction, and development of single-family and multi-family housing, along with supporting infrastructure. Working closely with clients, stakeholders, consultants, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams, you'll drive successful project delivery from planning and design through construction, turnover, and closeout while maintaining alignment with project goals, schedules, budgets, and governance requirements.

What You'll Do

Lead the planning, development, and delivery of residential construction and housing improvement programs throughout Florida.
Support annual capital investment planning efforts, including project prioritization, budgeting, forecasting, and cost estimating coordination.
Oversee the rehabilitation, demolition, reconstruction, and development of residential communities, including single-family and multi-family housing.
Manage architectural, engineering, planning, and consulting firms through procurement, contract negotiation, design development, permitting, and construction documentation.
Coordinate with client and project teams to ensure successful project execution while maintaining project scope, schedule, budget, quality, and risk objectives.
Assist clients with procurement strategies, contractor selection, and construction contract negotiations.
Direct construction activities through project turnover, occupancy, commissioning, and contract closeout.
Monitor and report on project performance, budget changes, schedule impacts, and key program risks to executive stakeholders.
Develop, implement, and maintain program management plans, workflows, procedures, and guidance documentation.
Engage Jacobs technical specialists and subject matter experts to support project delivery and resolve complex technical challenges.
Support executive leadership with strategic planning, resource management, community outreach, policy development, and program governance activities.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field; direct, relevant industry experience as an Owner's Representative, Residential Contractor, Residential Developer, or similar leadership role may be considered in lieu of a degree.20+ years of experience in residential construction, community planning, infrastructure development, design management, and construction management.
Experience serving as an Owner's Representative, Residential Contractor, Residential Developer, Program Manager, or similar leadership role overseeing projects from planning through construction and turnover.
Demonstrated experience managing large-scale residential development, housing rehabilitation, or community infrastructure programs.
Experience managing project scope, schedule, budget, consultant teams, procurement activities, and construction contracts.
Experience in engineering or construction management, business management, and financial planning.
Current certification from CMAA, AACE, or PMI required. CMAA certification is strongly preferred.

Ideally, you'll also have

Professional Engineer (PE) license.
Certified Construction Manager (CCM) certification.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
Certified General Contractor credential.
Experience leading large-scale housing redevelopment, mixed-use residential, affordable housing, or master-planned community projects.
Experience managing multidisciplinary teams across multiple concurrent projects and stakeholders.

This position is based onsite at our Davie, Florida office. Remote and hybrid work arrangements are not available for this role. This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $250,000.00 to $330,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on September 14, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

Onsite employees are expected to attend a Jacobs Workplace on a full-time basis, as required by the nature of their role.
